clue.text: One of the best from Felix stowe?

definitions.text: One of the best from Felix stowe?

parts.words: One of the best from Felix stowe?
parts.note: a sporting, generous person, read again as praise for Felixstowe as a fine harbour town

explanation.surface: A question about the finest thing to come out of a Suffolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: Felixstowe is a container port in Suffolk, England; split as the clue prints it, it invites the solver to think of a decent sea harbour as well as a decent sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes losing in good humour is praised as one of the best, and the phrase also ends in a word for a harbour.

clue.text: Show endurance in a marathon

parts.note: the runner with most stamina in a long race finishes ahead of rivals

explanation.surface: Advice to a distance runner to keep going to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting longer than rivals in a long race means beating them over the distance, the verb's literal sense.

clue.text: Invention of a number I note in the river

indicators.note: the small pieces sit inside the river's name, splitting it after its second letter

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England
V is the Roman numeral five
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone describes a contraption involving a figure and a note found in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A device is a contrivance or gadget someone has devised, which is an invention.

clue.text: Writer on a rickety steed in an Eastern state

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a nag is a broken-down old horse

explanation.surface: An author rides a shaky horse somewhere in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places the writer before the horse in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Penang is one of the constituent states of Malaysia, in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Exercise that keeps the doctor going from day to day

definitions.text: Exercise that keeps the doctor going from day to day

parts.words: Exercise that keeps the doctor going from day to day
parts.note: a daily workout seems meant, but it is a physician's steady list of patients that keeps the surgery busy

explanation.surface: Daily exercise keeps a doctor healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercise' suggests fitness, but the doctor's 'practice' is the medical business, and a regular one gives a steady income.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitual rehearsal of a skill is one sense; a GP's established surgery with steady patients is the other.

clue.text: With Gary the correction may be made at once

indicators.note: a correction changes the order, so the letters of the name phrase are rearranged

parts.note: the printed words taken letter for letter, plus the A the setter meant to include

explanation.surface: Someone promises that Gary will help fix a mistake immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With Gary' supplies only eight letters; the anagram needs an extra A, so the clue as printed is a letter short, probably a dropped 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something immediately, without delay, is doing it straight off.

clue.text: Riddle takes less than a second; yet it's puzzling

parts.note: an enigma is a riddle or mystery

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A riddle is solved in under a second, yet still baffles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mysterious and hard to understand is puzzling.

clue.text: Overwhelmed and united afresh

indicators.note: these two words are made anew, so their letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone is flooded with emotion at being reunited.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooded with more than one can handle is being swamped.

clue.text: Small and dainty opera by Thomas

definitions.meaning: a French word for petite and delicate
the 1866 opera by Ambroise Thomas, based on Goethe

explanation.surface: A dainty little opera by a composer called Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: The French adjective means petite and delicate, and it is also the title of Ambroise Thomas's best-known opera.

clue.text: Nevertheless the coach covers a town near Hitchin

indicators.note: the coach's word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a stage, short for stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach
even, as in 'even so', means nevertheless

explanation.surface: Despite everything, the coach serves a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stevenage and Hitchin are neighbouring towns in Hertfordshire, north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenage is a new town in Hertfordshire a few miles from Hitchin.

clue.text: Display sawn-off weapon for a big shot in Japan

indicators.note: the word is cut off at its end, losing its last letter

parts.note: to show is to display
a gun is a weapon

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a sawn-off shotgun to impress a Japanese gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sawn-off' wants to describe the weapon, like a sawn-off shotgun, but it trims the display word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was the hereditary military ruler of feudal Japan, the most powerful figure in the land.

clue.text: Belt a Knight Bachelor, we hear

indicators.note: the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: a knight is called Sir, and a bachelor is single

explanation.surface: A belt is said to belong to a knight who never married.
explanation.walkthrough: Knight Bachelor is also a real British honour, the lowest grade of knighthood, which disguises the split into SIR and SINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcingle is a girth strap round a horse's body, a kind of band holding a saddle or blanket.

clue.text: Where Father meets a man in recession

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about where Dad met a man during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' looks economic but turns 'a man' around; the bare 'Where' is the definition, answered by a place.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a place, the Central American country, so it answers the question word.

clue.text: He helps to shed the load

definitions.text: He helps to shed the load

parts.words: He helps to shed the load
parts.note: sounds like someone easing a burden, but describes a docker unloading ships' cargo

explanation.surface: Someone helps a person lighten their burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A docker who loads and unloads cargo from ships helps take off a vessel's freight.

clue.text: Sharp encounter between professional mourners?

definitions.meaning: keeners were hired to wail at funerals, so a contest between them

explanation.surface: A fierce contest between people paid to grieve.
explanation.definitionFit: An eager, closely fought contest; and, whimsically, a game played by those who keen, meaning wail for the dead.

clue.text: Heavenly body in which evergreens take preference

indicators.note: the evergreens sit inside the heavenly body

parts.note: a comet is a heavenly body
firs are evergreen trees

explanation.surface: A comet in which fir trees are given priority.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put ahead of everything else is to take priority.

clue.text: To is human, to forgive divine" (Pope)

definitions.text: To is human, to forgive divine" (Pope)

parts.words: To is human, to forgive divine" (Pope)
parts.note: the famous line from Pope's Essay on Criticism with its verb left out, to be supplied

explanation.surface: A quotation from Alexander Pope about human failing and forgiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing word in Pope's line is the answer; the gap is part of the clue's design.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope's line says making mistakes is human, so the gap wants the verb meaning to make a mistake.

clue.text: Greek character in due time

definitions.meaning: the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet
estimated time of arrival, when something is expected

explanation.surface: A Greek person arrives when expected.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a letter of the Greek alphabet and the abbreviation for estimated time of arrival.

clue.text: Butter or batter

definitions.meaning: something that butts, a male sheep
to batter is to strike hard

explanation.surface: Two kitchen words, one letter apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A male sheep butts with its head, and to strike or force something violently is to ram it.

clue.text: Could be Earth's ideal spot-vacated by Adam and Eve

definitions.text: Could be Earth's ideal spot-vacated by Adam and Eve

indicators.note: the phrase could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A description of Eden as the perfect place on earth that the first couple had to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Earth's' counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden, the perfect garden Adam and Eve were expelled from, is the paradise lost of Milton's epic.

clue.text: Provide equipment for a member

explanation.surface: Kitting out a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip with weapons, and a limb such as an upper limb, which is one of the body's members.

clue.text: Gloss over

parts.note: reads as a verb, to hide faults, but is a noun: a thin shiny layer over something

explanation.definitionFit: A thin decorative layer laid on top of cheaper wood gives a glossy surface hiding what is beneath.

clue.text: As 27 proved with dispatch

parts.note: the brute of 27 across murdered Nancy in Oliver Twist; dispatch means killing

explanation.surface: A character proved himself efficient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with dispatch' sounds like promptly, but to dispatch is to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Sikes murders Nancy in Oliver Twist, showing himself a murderer.

clue.text: Indifferent about a loss

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a miss is a failure, a loss

explanation.surface: Someone is unbothered by a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless and negligent about duties is lax, which is close to indifferent.

clue.text: To divide a quarter is hard

parts.note: to sever is to cut apart
E, east, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Splitting something into quarters is difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh and strict, as in a stern punishment, is hard.

clue.text: Man of letters in times past

definitions.text: Man of letters in times past

parts.words: Man of letters in times past
parts.note: suggests an old author, but means a professional copyist or clerk who wrote documents

explanation.surface: A description of a historical literary figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Before printing and typewriters, a clerk or notary wrote out letters and documents for others.

clue.text: That is costly to start with, love

indicators.note: the costly word is placed at the beginning

parts.note: dear means expensive
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone tells their sweetheart that something is expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment, like sweetheart, used to address a loved one.

clue.text: Dickensian brute accounts for US presidents?

parts.note: bills are accounts to be paid
Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A villain is behind invoices sent to American leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: The violent burglar of Oliver Twist is Dickens's most notorious thug.

clue.text: Finds traces of further mould

indicators.note: the letters are found in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone discovers signs of more fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mould' suggests fungus, but here it is a verb, to shape again.
explanation.definitionFit: To recast is to cast again, giving metal or an idea a fresh shape.

clue.text: Made up for changed gear

definitions.meaning: put on different clothes, dressed again

explanation.surface: Someone compensated by changing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting right a wrong is to remedy it, and dressing again is putting on clothing once more.
